# Google Interview Experience For SWE Internship (Off-campus)

Last Updated : 28 May, 2024

## Application Process:

I applied for the Google software engineering internship at the Google career portal without any referral. The internship application process at Google consisted of four rounds:

1. Resume Shortlisting
2. Telephonic Round (30 minutes)
3. Technical Interview 1 (45 minutes)
4. Technical Interview 2 (45 minutes)

### Round 1: Resume Shortlisting

I attached my resume with all the details of my coursework, projects, and other relevant experience; fortunately, it was shortlisted for the subsequent round.

### Round 2: Telephonic Round

This round consisted of a 30-minute call with a Google interviewer. The subject of discussion was more behavioural and introductory questions

Some of the questions that were asked:

* "Tell me about yourself and why you are interested in this role?"
* "How are you a better candidate than others?"
* "Describe a challenging situation you faced and how you handled it.".

In an attempt to provide brief yet detailed responses that demonstrate my problem-solving abilities about my education as well as my experience; it turns out though that my answers fell short.

****Verdict:**** Rejected

title: Chat Activity: Most Active Users
reported: Design a chat system with an API to record a conversation between two users at a timestamp and an API returning the most active users (most unique partners, each pair counted once); follow-ups: top K, access modifiers, and thread safety of the hash map.

sources.passage:
Google preliminary interview L4
I was asked the following:

Design a chat system with two APIs:

- An API to register a conversation event between two users at a specific timestamp.
- An API to return the most active users.

Here, “active” means the user who has had conversations with the highest number of unique users, and each conversation between a pair of users should only be counted once.

I implemented a solution and also handled the follow-up requirement of returning the top K most active users. I covered edge cases and discussed the overall design in detail and the interviewer was satisfied with it.

However, I struggled with two follow-up questions:

- A basic OOP question about private/public access levels. I mentioned using getters/setters, but forgot that within the same class they’re not necessary.
A-  multithreading question: my solution used unordered_map in C++, and I didn’t mention/know that it is not thread-safe or how to handle concurrency.

My question:
How much would these two weak answers impact my chances of moving to the next stage, given that I solved the main problem thoroughly?

### Googliness Round

I was asked standard behavioral questions with follow-ups.

One question I struggled with was:

**"If a project is unclear or there is ambiguity, how would you handle it?"**

I couldn't structure my response properly. I stumbled over my words and went in a different direction instead of answering the question clearly.

I recognize that I could have communicated my approach better in this round.

### Final Feedback

Unfortunately, I received a rejection.

The recruiter mentioned that I needed to **strengthen my technical concepts and practice more LeetCode problems**.

I'm a little confused about the technical feedback because:

- My Part 1 BFS approach and implementation were accepted.
- For Part 2, I struggled to understand the question despite asking for clarification.
- The interviewer acknowledged that my proposed approach could work but didn't ask me to implement it.
- I also recognize that my communication during one Googliness question could have been better.

I understand that an accepted approach doesn't necessarily mean the overall interview met the L4 bar.

**Has anyone experienced something similar in a Google L4 interview? How much do ambiguous follow-ups, incomplete implementation of Part 2, and communication during Googliness affect the final decision?**

I'd appreciate any feedback or suggestions for improving before my next attempt.

My SDE Android Internship Interview Experience at Groww (2025)
I recently got the opportunity to interview for the SDE Android Intern role at Groww.

I had applied through a Google Form on **13th May 2025**, and on **25th June 2025**, I received an assignment to build a stock display app using Kotlin (everyone who applied received the same assignment). I submitted it on **4th July 2025**, and got an interview call from HR on **22nd July 2025**.

During the interview, most of the discussion revolved around the assignment. I began by explaining the app, its architecture, and why I chose the MVVM pattern with Repository. I was asked:

	•	What happens when the user rotates the screen?
	•	What are lambda functions and their use cases?
	•	How did I implement the bottom navigation bar?
	•	What is dependency injection?
	•	How does my ViewModel help retain data across screen rotations?
	•	What is the Activity lifecycle?

I was also given a scenario:
*If a screen shows a RecyclerView with payment options like PhonePe and Cash on Delivery, how would I ensure that only one card is selected at a time? I had to explain how I would manage selection and persist the user’s choice.*

There were also several questions around data handling. I explained that I implemented caching — if data is in the cache, I use it; otherwise, I make an API call. I was asked where I handled the logic to validate the cache and how I structured my API calls.

The interviewer also asked me about the numbers mentioned in my resume — how I calculated them and what they represented.

Again, the discussion went kinda deep into the implementation details.

Some of the questions were:

* Explain the OTP lifecycle in your project.
* How would you handle multiple users?
* How did you ensure concurrency?
* How did you implement chats in your project?
* How does the system behave when multiple requests arrive simultaneously?

And there were quite a few follow-up questions for each of these.

****System Design****

There was also a basic system design question:

* How would you design an Event Management System?

The discussion included things like:

* Overall architecture
* Entities
* APIs
* Database
* Concurrency
* Transactional functionality

The interviewer also asked me to explain the transactional functionality in detail, followed by a few scenario-based questions and follow-ups.

### HR Questions

Some of the questions were:

* What is your strongest domain in tech?
* Rate yourself in your strongest domain out of 5.
* What is your weakest domain in tech?
* Where do you see yourself in the next 5 years, technically and non-technically?
* Why Groww?
* What's your dream company?
* How would you deal with disputes within a team?

And, there were follow-ups for almost every answer.

That was my Groww on-campus interview experience :)
